title: Split work and rework in the sidecar, cost and review
goal: Work lines carry rework counts from the first refused done; backlog.py cost --rework prints them and /kb-sprint review lists items with rework.

gates.question: Is an item line's rework block a part of the line's own counts (work = line minus rework), or counts added to them?
options: A part of the line's counts: the line keeps the whole window total, rework is a subset, work is computed
Added: the line holds only the work counts and rework is a separate block
gates.recommendation: A part of the line's counts: the line keeps the whole window total, rework is a subset, work is computed
gates.answer: A part of the line's counts: the line keeps the whole window total, rework is a subset, work is computed

gates.question: Which prompt starts rework: the one whose done was first refused, or the next one?
options: The prompt that ran the first refused done: from that prompt on counts as rework
The prompt after it: the refusing prompt stays work
gates.recommendation: The prompt that ran the first refused done: from that prompt on counts as rework
gates.answer: The prompt that ran the first refused done: from that prompt on counts as rework

gates.question: Does cost --rework print on top of the usual cost report, or instead of it?
options: On top: the usual report unchanged, then a work and rework block (json: an added rework_split key)
Instead: only the work and rework figures
gates.recommendation: On top: the usual report unchanged, then a work and rework block (json: an added rework_split key)
gates.answer: On top: the usual report unchanged, then a work and rework block (json: an added rework_split key)

notes: Touches carry the cost row of tools.md (new flag) and usage.md (work line shape); the push gate refuses the code without them.
